caption: Medical aid, meds and copayments take a third of what we earn. What does health cost your household?

slides.title:
What staying healthy
costs us on
R35 600 p/m
Living in Standerton
slides.body:
Male, 49
Married, two teens (17 and 14)
Job: Foreman, brickworks (his wife has type 2 diabetes)
Net salary: R35 600 p/m

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.body: I've had the plan for 22 years. It's the one thing I won't downgrade.

slides.title: Out-of-pocket health
slides.includes: Wife's diabetes supplies, my BP tablets, spectacles, dentist copayments
slides.body: The plan pays some of it. The rest comes at the pharmacy till.

slides.title: Bond
slides.body: Four years left. The house is the only thing on this list that ends.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: Brown bread and fresh vegetables cost more. She notices and I notice.

slides.title: School
slides.includes: Fees, uniforms, extra lessons for matric
slides.body: Maths tutor is R600 of it. My son asked for it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, electricity, phones & TV, funeral policy, stokvel, black tax, the club
slides.body: The club is R900 on Fridays. That's the one my wife has opinions about.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R35 600. Health, the bond and groceries alone are almost two thirds of it.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon and it put the pharmacy, the doctor and the medical aid in one place.

I had never added them up.

No bank login needed.
